diagnosis:
I calibrated HBV on the full record (Oct 1971 to Dec 1997, after a one-year warm-up) using DDS with NSE as the objective. The fit is good: NSE 0.885, KGE 0.91, r 0.94. Simulated flow is about 5% higher than observed (PBIAS +5.3%), so the model may slightly overestimate summer baseflow and low flows.

To test transfer, I calibrated a separate copy on 1971–1985 (NSE 0.896) and ran it on 1985–1997 (NSE 0.868, KGE 0.92). The two calibrations gave similar values for most parameters. The final model has a large, fairly nonlinear soil store (FC about 450 mm, BETA about 6, LP 0.83). Quick runoff (K0 0.71, K1 0.22, UZL 31) and a moderately fast groundwater store (K2 0.073, PERC 5.8) fit this small, low-permeability Cornish catchment, which responds quickly. MAXBAS is about 2 days.

Weak points are probably the highest flood peaks, low-flow timing in dry summers, and the autumn wetting-up when the soil store refills. Snow parameters are essentially unconstrained because snow is negligible here, and a few of them (SFCF, CWH, CFMAX in the early-period run) ended at their range limits. Some of the soil and response parameters also trade off against each other. Even so, I'm fairly confident the model will reach a daily NSE of about 0.85 to 0.88 in 1998–2008.
